core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aasmaa corresponds to Arabic أسماء, the plural of اسم (“name/noun”); it does not lexically mean “sky/heaven.”
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Plural of اسم (name); the specific personal-name interpretation is separate from the lexical plural.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Lane's Lexicon explicitly gives أَسْمَاءٌ as a plural of اِسْمٌ, “name.” The former “sky/heaven” gloss was a conflation with سَمَاء (sky/heaven), a different Arabic word with similar spelling/root history. The association with Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr is a historical bearer claim, not the word's plural meaning.

faq.a: The Arabic form أسماء is the plural of اسم, meaning “name.” It does not mean “sky/heaven”; that is سماء.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aasmaa?
faq.a: The recorded form أسماء is Arabic and is documented as the plural of اسم.
The form أسماء is Arabic; whether a particular person uses it as a given name is a separate usage question.

faq.q: What is the root of Aasmaa?
faq.a: Lane's Lexicon associates اسم with the root سمو; the plural is أسماء.
Asmāʾ has historical use as a personal name in Muslim history, including Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr; that is distinct from a religious prescription.
This record does not claim that the personal name is specifically named in the Qur'an; lexical and historical evidence should be kept distinct.

A rough guide is “as-maa”; Arabic pronunciation and romanization conventions may vary.

faq.a: It is commonly used as a feminine personal name in some Muslim communities, but regional frequency data has not been supplied.
